key_insight: Targeted synthetic images generated from simple task keywords (e.g., “Depth Order”) can teach vision-language models low-level visual perception skills—improving spatial understanding and viewpoint recognition where natural images fall short.
problem_solved: VLMs lack reliable supervision for low-level visual perception (spatial relations, depth ordering, viewpoint) because natural image datasets provide limited, noisy, or untargeted signals for these tasks.
method: Task-aware synthetic data generation: produce controllable, annotated images conditioned on a single task keyword (e.g., Depth Order).
Diverse, parameterized scene synthesis: vary geometry, lighting, occlusion, and viewpoints to cover targeted visual cues.
Integrate synthetic supervision into VLM training/fine-tuning and evaluate on perception benchmarks to measure improvements.
impact: Provides a practical, scalable way to close perception gaps in VLMs by adding low-cost, targeted synthetic supervision—enabling better spatial reasoning, more robust multimodal models, and faster iteration for practitioners.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: keyword → synthetic scene generator → annotated images → VLM fine-tuning (arrow flow).
Before/After bar chart: performance on spatial/viewpoint tasks (baseline vs. VisionFoundry).
Grid of synthetic examples: controlled variations (depth layers, viewpoints, occlusions) with labels.
Attention/heatmap overlay on an image: illustrate improved spatial reasoning or correct depth ordering.
paper_title: VisionFoundry: Teaching VLMs Visual Perception with Synthetic Images
paper_authors: Guanyu Zhou, Yida Yin, Wenhao Chai, Shengbang Tong, Xingyu Fu
